result.summary: Extracts block download scheduling, tracking, and peer state from `PeerManagerImpl` and `CNodeState` into a dedicated `BlockDownloadManager` module. The new manager mirrors the pimpl design of `TxDownloadManager` while keeping synchronization under `cs_main`. Isolated unit tests and a new fuzz target are added to exercise the extracted state machine and invariants.
result.problem: `net_processing.cpp` is over 6,000 lines long and conflates distinct peer-to-peer subsystems into `PeerManagerImpl`, making block download state transitions, stalling logic, and availability tracking difficult to reason about, review, or test in isolation without spinning up full node harnesses.
evidence: Shrinks `net_processing.cpp` by 442 net lines and removes 10 block-tracking fields from `CNodeState` (PR description).

Enables isolated verification via 8 unit test cases and a new fuzz target exercising download scheduling, in-flight accounting, stalling, and post-disconnect cleanup (`test/fuzz/blockdownloadman.cpp`).
Continues the modularization pattern previously accepted in #30110 (`TxDownloadManager`) (PR description).
result.scope_notes: The diff includes a large mechanical call-site migration (~150 call sites) across `net_processing.cpp`, plus ~800 lines of new unit and fuzz tests. The new module intentionally does not introduce its own mutex, remaining under `cs_main`.
result.card: Extracts block download state and scheduling logic from PeerManagerImpl and CNodeState into a new BlockDownloadManager module. net_processing.cpp conflates multiple P2P subsystems into a single 6,200-line file, making block download logic difficult to test or review independently. Following the pimpl pattern established by TxDownloadManager, this refactor retains cs_main locking while adding isolated unit tests and a fuzz target. It has no PR dependencies.
